definitions.explanation: A long, thin piece of wood or other material.
A straight line drawn on paper.

examples.japanese: {棒|ぼう}で{地面|じめん}に{線|せん}を{引|ひ}いた。
examples.english: I drew a line on the ground with a stick.

examples.japanese: {鉄|てつ}{棒|ぼう}にぶら{下|さ}がる。
examples.english: To hang from an iron bar.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{棒|ぼう}を{振|ふ}り{回|まわ}して{遊|あそ}んでいる。
examples.english: The child is playing by swinging a stick around.

examples.japanese: せっかくの{努力|どりょく}を{棒|ぼう}に{振|ふ}ってしまった。
examples.english: I ended up wasting all my hard work.
examples.notes: {棒|ぼう}に{振|ふ}る = to waste, throw away

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}の{上|うえ}に{棒|ぼう}を{引|ひ}いて{消|け}した。
examples.english: I crossed out the name by drawing a line over it.

examples.japanese: {棒読|ぼうよ}みで{台詞|せりふ}を{言|い}った。
examples.english: I said the lines in a monotone.
examples.notes: {棒読|ぼうよ}み = flat, monotone reading

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{棒|ぼう}と{青|あお}い{棒|ぼう}で{比較|ひかく}を{表|あらわ}すグラフを{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I drew a graph that shows the comparison using red and blue bars.

notes:
A basic word with many compound uses.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
・{鉄棒|てつぼう} (horizontal bar - gymnastics)
・{棒|ぼう}グラフ (bar graph)
・{泥棒|どろぼう} (thief)
・{相棒|あいぼう} (partner, sidekick)
・{棒読|ぼうよ}み (monotone reading)
・{棒|ぼう}に{振|ふ}る (to waste, throw away)

IDIOMS:
・{棒|ぼう}に{振|ふ}る (to waste something - effort, money)
・{犬|いぬ}も{歩|ある}けば{棒|ぼう}に{当|あ}たる (A dog that walks will bump into a stick - you'll encounter fortune/misfortune if you go out)
